name: Flaring suture (alar flaring)

card.summary: A suture technique in rhinoplasty that reshapes the nostril or nasal valve area, used to adjust how the nose and nostrils look.
card.note: Surgical; over-correction can affect breathing and symmetry.

quick.overview:
Flaring sutures are stitches placed during rhinoplasty to shape cartilage at the side of the nose. In functional rhinoplasty they widen the internal nasal valve; in aesthetic discussions people use the term for shaping the nostril flare.

The appearance payoff is a nose and nostril outline closer to what the patient wants, from the front or base view. It is performed by a surgeon within a wider nasal procedure.
quick.how: The surgeon places sutures in nasal cartilage, often alongside other manoeuvres such as spreader grafts, during an open or closed rhinoplasty under anaesthesia.
quick.risks: Overly aggressive nasal surgery can cause breathing problems, asymmetry, collapse or a pinched tip, and revision is needed in roughly 5–20 percent of rhinoplasties. Swelling can take a year to settle.

lead: Flaring sutures are used in rhinoplasty alongside spreader grafts to widen the internal nasal valve; a valve angle greater than 15 degrees is described as needed for unobstructed breathing.[1] In the looksmaxxing context, the term also refers to shaping how much the nostrils flare.
The nasal alar base is one of nine aesthetic subunits of the nose, and published techniques exist to reduce it, such as a 2023 modified alar base reduction technique.[1][2]

angle.text: The sutures reposition cartilage so the nostril and side of the nose take a different shape, as part of a wider rhinoplasty plan.

paras: Rhinoplasty may be open or closed, with approach depending on surgeon expertise and anatomy; meta-analyses report no significant long-term difference in functional scores between them.[1]
Reported complications of aggressive nasal surgery include breathing problems, asymmetry, collapse, a pinched tip and a scooped nose; smoking compromises healing.[1]

No studies found specific to flaring sutures for cosmetic nostril shaping. Related work includes a technique paper on modified alar base reduction[2] and a study of nasal ala anatomy for neurotoxin injection.[3]
